_comment: Phase 2, seeded before the full ~40-case physical golden set (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md §6). Two case types: 'query' cases run a pipeline end-to-end and check retrieved + recommended frames against hard constraints (no LLM judge). 'catalog_composition' and 'derivation_function' cases check the contested thresholds in app/lib/config/thresholds.ts directly, independent of any pipeline.

query_cases.query: Titanium frames under 8000 rupees, in stock
query_cases.note: Control case -- a query where valid candidates are plentiful enough that naive retrieval can land on a correct answer by chance.

Targets catalog intentional gap #1 (validate.py asserts this combination is empty). Correct answer: name the violated constraint and offer the nearest alternative, not a bare refusal -- see decisions.md 2026-08-28, 'refusal framing correction'.

Targets catalog intentional gap #3. Ideal answer recommends Nira Edition 292 (the nearest miss, ₹4,600, a ₹100 overage -- see evals/golden/refusal.json's gap3-titanium-under-4500 case for the generated nearest_miss data) and names the overage explicitly rather than burying it. An earlier version of this note said Basalt Form 448 at ₹4,800 was the nearest miss -- that was inherited from what the naive baseline happened to retrieve, not computed from the catalog, and was wrong (Basalt is tied for 2nd cheapest at ₹4,800; Nira Edition 292 is the true cheapest at ₹4,600). See decisions.md 2026-08-28, 'golden set ground truth was circular.'

Not an intentional gap -- just far out of range. Not a test of whether the pipeline refuses (the gpt-5.6-luna re-run showed it doesn't reliably -- docs/phase1-baseline-failures.md, 'Better prose, worse compliance'), and per PROJECT_CONTEXT.md §6 bare refusal isn't the target behavior anyway. This entry only checks hard-constraint compliance of whatever gets recommended, same as every other case here; the framing question (does it name the constraint and offer the real nearest sports-tagged frame, per evals/golden/refusal.json's sports-under-500 case) is graded there, not here.

catalog_composition_cases.description: How many progressive_ready frames clear the lens-height floor at the old (30mm), current (32mm), and optician-cited (44mm) thresholds.

derivation_function_cases.description: At rx_power = -3.5D, does app/lib/derivation.ts#deriveRimTypeConstraint require non-rimless construction under the old (-4.00D), current (-3.00D), and optician-cited (-2.00D) thresholds?
